answer.submission_route:
The patient can submit an appeal using the following routes:
- By Mail: UPMC Health Plan, Attn: Complaints and Grievances, PO Box 2939, Pittsburgh, PA 15230-2939
- By Fax: 1-412-454-7920
- By Phone: Call the Health Care Concierge / Member Services number on the back of the member ID card, or toll-free at 1-888-876-2756 (TTY: 711)
- By Email: HealthPlanCompliance@upmc.edu
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Because UPMC Health Plan utilizes proprietary InterQual® criteria sets (specifically 'InterQual® CP: Procedures: Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Knee' for CPT 29881) under Policy CRM.003, the specific checklists are not publicly published in full. The patient can obtain the exact applied criteria by calling UPMC Health Plan Member Services (or the phone number on their ID card) to request a copy of the criteria used to make their medical necessity determination.
answer.notes: UPMC Health Plan transitioned to using proprietary InterQual® Connect criteria sets to review musculoskeletal/orthopedic procedures (such as knee arthroscopy and meniscectomy). Typical InterQual requirements for knee arthroscopy/meniscectomy (CPT 29881) include: (1) Symptoms of a meniscal tear such as persistent knee pain, swelling, or mechanical symptoms (locking, catching, or giving way); (2) Physical examination findings such as joint line tenderness or a positive McMurray test; (3) Failure of conservative therapy (NSAIDs, physical therapy, activity modification, or injections) typically for 4 to 6 weeks; (4) MRI confirmation of a meniscal tear that correlates with symptoms; and (5) Absence of advanced or severe knee osteoarthritis (e.g., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4), in which arthroscopy is considered not medically necessary.
